title: Constructor with Hidden Heavy Side-Effects (Opaque RAII)
pattern: Performing heavy, blocking, or asynchronous operations (like spawning threads, opening file descriptors, or initiating TCP connections) inside a standard initializer or constructor.
why_bad: Constructors are expected to be cheap, predictable, and side-effect-free heap or stack allocations. Hiding structural side-effects inside constructors leads to resource leaks, test flakiness, and hard-to-trace concurrent race conditions.
detection: A constructor method (e.g., `new()`) containing thread spawns, blocking file I/O, or network connections.
counterexample: Smart pointers or memory buffer allocations where resource reservation is the explicit, documented purpose of the type (e.g., `Vec::with_capacity`).
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 18, "Code Should Be Obvious" (p. 148).
